sources: Guards of Atlantis II rulebook, 2nd printing (Wolff Designa PDF; printed pp. 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23) as summarised in docs/DOMAIN.md

Counters are looked up by heroes in play (seats), an app decision documented in docs/DOMAIN.md; the rulebook's per-player values (lifeCountersByPlayers, listedFromPlayers, requiredFromPlayers) label where that house rule differs

rulesNote.title: Double lane rules (rulebook p.20)
points: Considerably more challenging than a single lane: everyone should know the game well.
Each lane has its own Battle Zone, minions and Wave counters. Minions stay bound to the Battle Zone they first spawned in.
With more than 3 heroes per team, the extra heroes start in empty spaces next to their team's occupied hero spawn points.
On cards, "the Battle Zone" means "a Battle Zone".
The two Minion Battles are resolved separately, at the same time.
After the last Wave counter on either lane flips, the team with more total Zones between its Throne and both Battle Zones wins.
If a push would make both teams win at once, spawn all minions back in the Zones they held before the push and keep playing.

layouts.guidance: Each player controls 2 heroes; use the 4-player setup. The rulebook warns this is considerably more challenging and takes longer to finish.
The most experienced player controls 2 heroes and replaces the Gold card of one of them with its Handicap card.
Each hero on the larger team replaces one of its basic cards with its Handicap card.
House rule: one player on the smaller team controls 2 heroes, so both teams field 3.
Each hero on the larger team replaces one of its basic cards with its Handicap card.
House rule: one player on the smaller team controls 2 heroes, so both teams field 4.
Each hero on the larger team replaces one of its basic cards with its Handicap card.
House rule: one player on the smaller team controls 2 heroes, so both teams field 5.

endOfRound.title: Minion Battle
endOfRound.detail: The team with fewer minions in the Battle Zone removes the difference (its choice; the Heavy minion goes last). Equal numbers: no effect.

endOfRound.title: Remove Tokens, Return Markers
endOfRound.detail: Remove all tokens from the board. Return all markers to the supply.

endOfRound.title: Push the Lane
endOfRound.detail: If a team has no minions left in the Battle Zone, the other team wins the push: flip a Wave counter (the last one ends the game, push winner wins). The Battle Zone moves one Zone toward the loser's Throne (their Throne Zone: push winner wins); respawn minions there.

endOfRound.title: Retrieve Cards
endOfRound.detail: Take back all your resolved and discarded cards. This cancels all your Active effects, including "Next Turn" effects.

endOfRound.title: Level Up
endOfRound.detail: Mandatory: if you have enough coins, buy as many levels as you can afford. Everyone leveling up upgrades at the same time.

endOfRound.title: Collect a Pity Coin
endOfRound.detail: Everyone who did not level up this round takes 1 coin. You can't level up this round, even if you now have enough.

tieBreaker: Cross-team initiative tie: one of the tied players on the team showing acts first. After resolving their card, that player (and only that player) flips the coin to the other side (p.7).
Same-team tie: the team agrees who goes first without discussing why. Don't flip the coin (pp.4, 7).
The team showing also goes first, without flipping, when the order matters for simultaneous Active effects (p.17) or for minions moved back into the Battle Zone (p.18).
It also places first when minions can't respawn on a blocked Spawn point (p.8).
extendedCountNote: Odd counts and 8 to 10 players are recommended only when everyone has played at least 5 times.
firstGameAdvice: If anyone is new, the rulebook suggests a Quick game.
